products.section_lead: N30 for private executive pods. N45 for premium network commuting when seat demand is real.

items.title: N30 Executive Shuttle
items.body: Your team’s boat — point to point, no waiting for other companies. Fixed AM/PM slots with a wait buffer for executives, Wi‑Fi and tables so people can work, coffee and light F&B included. One captain runs the vessel and hospitality on this small craft.

items.title: N45 Commuter Line
items.body: N45 Commuter Line — 30 seats, scheduled service on a fixed line. Launches when a line reaches roughly 60–80 committed seats.

anchor.title: Option A — Sponsor a line
anchor.body: Your institution underwrites a scheduled service — indicative from ~$125K per month. Non-binding. Helps us light the right line first.

seats.title: Option B — Commit seats
seats.body: Reserve seats at $750–900 per seat-month and we aggregate launch demand for your line. Non-binding.

executive.title: Option C — N30 executive program
executive.body: Reserve fixed AM/PM dedicated slots for your team only — all-in trip price with Wi‑Fi cabin and F&B. Non-binding interest.

copy.hero_headline: One terminal. The whole harbor network.
copy.hero_sub: Electric hydrofoil lines across the harbor, Long Island Sound, and Connecticut — meeting at transfer hubs. Your campus only needs a stop on the water. Employees board near home, transfer once if needed, and arrive at work.

problem_chips.label: Congestion toll into the Manhattan CBD
Your campus plugs into the full network

copy.precedent: New York institutions already fund employee transportation at scale — intercampus shuttles, guaranteed-ride programs, tenant buses. One of the city's largest hospital systems already runs an employee water shuttle. The behavior is proven. What's been missing is a vessel built for it.
copy.stripe_lesson: New York institutions already fund employee transportation at scale. We ran the first employer water commute on San Francisco Bay — the ride worked; the vessel class was the lesson. A non-binding letter of intent sequences which harbor lines light first.
copy.loi_cta: Non-binding. Helps us sequence harbor lines to real demand at your terminal — and every origin that can transfer to you.
copy.price_anchor: $650–750 / seat-month where a ferry alternative exists · $750–900 where none does — often less than the parking + toll stack it replaces
copy.launch_trigger: A line advances when about 60–80 seats are committed on that corridor — enough for real commuter service.
copy.problem_title: The congestion charge is the tax. The water is the spare lane.
copy.problem_lead: Your people already live and work on the water. Roads and tolls take the rest. Electric hydrofoils cut that tax — terminal to terminal, above the traffic.
copy.proof_title: New York already funds the water commute.
copy.proof_lead: Institutions already pay for employee transportation. We bring the vessel class and a connected network.
copy.proof_worked_body: Intercampus shuttles and guaranteed-ride programs already exist at scale.
copy.proof_fixed_body: First employer water commute on SF Bay — ride worked; twenty-seat class is the product.
copy.proof_ask_body: Non-binding LOI — seats or line anchor — so we sequence on real demand.
copy.network_lead: Pick where your people live and where you work. We’ll show the water path — including transfers — and compare it to a typical AM peak drive. Gold rings are transfer hubs (Pier 11, E 34th, and more).
copy.map_detail_empty: Pick two terminals in Find my ride — or select a line or stop.
copy.calc_lead_html: Optional planning math. If you ran Find my ride, times can be prefilled from that route. Seat pricing is locked at $650–750 / month where a ferry alternative exists and $750–900 where none does. Defaults target $600 per rider net employer cost vs a $759 parking + toll benchmark.
copy.hero_note: Non-binding letter of intent · no commitment · helps us sequence which line launches first
copy.hero_cta_network: Find a route to my office
copy.network_footnote: Gold rings mark transfer hubs (Pier 11, E 34th, BPC, Paulus, E 90th). Landings are usable marina/pier berths. Expresses end at E 34th — transfer to the East River Line for Pier 11. Hudson is one spine (Yonkers through Jersey City to downtown).
copy.office_lead: You don’t sponsor every line. Sit on a hub — or a stop that feeds one — and riders transfer to you. Tap a campus to set it as your office and see origin coverage at launch vs full network.
copy.office_insight: Example: an LOI at Pier 11 still serves Hudson, Brooklyn, and Staten Island riders on day one — and Sound / Queens riders who transfer at E 34th.
copy.why_lead: The congestion charge is the tax. The harbor is the spare lane — terminal to terminal, above the traffic.

fn_exec_shuttle.text: Executive shuttle bands are indicative, backed out from N30 ~$1M capex, single-captain loaded wages, energy/maintenance/berth scaled from fleet planning, and all-in F&B. Fixed AM/PM slots assumed. Not a quote.
